title: BM/GURF/Steadman completeness inventory with BM readiness supplement
scope: Distinct families in 18 recovered historical inputs plus five additive proof/development notes (23 sources). Six new scoped results; full research completion not established.

schema.label: Defined
schema.meaning: An explicit mathematical object/type, contract or convention is stated.
schema.limit: Does not prove nonempty realization, physical reality or an independently calibrated native instance.

schema.label: Theorem
schema.meaning: A scoped result/counterexample has a written source proof, standard derivation or explicit accepted certificate.
schema.limit: All stated hypotheses remain necessary. This audit does not convert internal proof evidence into independent validation or novelty.

schema.label: Conditional theorem
schema.meaning: An implication is stated, but its native bridge, quantitative estimates or structured-descent assumptions are unestablished for the intended application.
schema.limit: Do not claim the consequent for that application until those obligations pass.

schema.label: Hypothesis
schema.meaning: A physical proposal, active theorem candidate, unresolved research question or reported result without recovered full proof.
schema.limit: A source gap is identified as a source gap, rather than proof that the original result is false.

schema.label: Physical interpretation
schema.meaning: A semantic/physical reading or translation of existing mathematics.
schema.limit: Requires extra physics and testable consequences to become a new physical law.

schema.label: Missing equation
schema.meaning: A demanded universal or iterative physical model lacks its governing quantitative/constitutive equation.
schema.limit: A missing proof or an ordinary unspecified application parameter is not automatically a missing fundamental equation.

inventory.name: Exact fibre factorization
inventory.statement: Classical theorem. For functions $R:X\to Z$ and $T:X\to W$, there exists a unique $D:R(X)\to W$ with $DR=T$ iff $R(x)=R(x')$ implies $T(x)=T(x')$.
inventory.assumptions: Use the exact domain and hypotheses in the statement; no native regularity or physical content is automatic.
inventory.evidence: Written argument recorded in source; not independently re-certified in this audit
inventory.clause: R: T01 Exact fibre factorization (line 2192)
inventory.remaining_work: Retain the stated hypotheses; no open obligation for this scoped statement. Independent validation is a separate evidence gate.

inventory.name: Passport sufficiency
inventory.statement: GURF corollary. In the deterministic observation sector, let $B_P:X\to Q_P$ collect the specified Passport observations. A task $T$ factors through $B_P$ iff $\ker B_P\subseteq\ker T$.
inventory.assumptions: Use the exact domain and hypotheses in the statement; no native regularity or physical content is automatic.
inventory.evidence: Written argument recorded in source; not independently re-certified in this audit
inventory.clause: R: T02 Passport sufficiency (line 2198)
inventory.remaining_work: Retain the stated hypotheses; no open obligation for this scoped statement. Independent validation is a separate evidence gate.

inventory.name: Completion fibre sufficiency
inventory.statement: GURF corollary. For a set-indexed family $r_\alpha$ whose product is defined, let $R(x)=(r_\alpha(x))_\alpha$. A task is recoverable exactly when it is constant on every nonempty $\bigcap_\alpha r_\alpha^{-1}(\ell_\alpha)$.
inventory.assumptions: Use the exact domain and hypotheses in the statement; no native regularity or physical content is automatic.
inventory.evidence: Written argument recorded in source; not independently re-certified in this audit
inventory.clause: R: T03 Completion fibre sufficiency (line 2204)
inventory.remaining_work: Retain the stated hypotheses; no open obligation for this scoped statement. Independent validation is a separate evidence gate.

inventory.name: Canonical exact task quotient
inventory.statement: Classical quotient theorem in BM scope. For a task family $\mathscr Q$, put $E_{\mathscr Q}=\bigcap_{T\in\mathscr Q}\ker T$. This is the coarsest equivalence whose quotient preserves every task. Any sufficient representation $R$ induces a unique map $h:R(X)\to X/E_{\mathscr Q}$ with $hR=q_{\mathscr Q}$.
inventory.assumptions: Use the exact domain and hypotheses in the statement; no native regularity or physical content is automatic.
inventory.evidence: Written argument recorded in source; not independently re-certified in this audit
inventory.clause: R: T04 Canonical exact task quotient (line 2210)
inventory.remaining_work: Retain the stated hypotheses; no open obligation for this scoped statement. Independent validation is a separate evidence gate.

inventory.name: Finite exact carrier bound

inventory.name: The scalar decoder theorem does not yet include uncertain codes
inventory.statement:
Let the task values t(x) be bounded real numbers. Instead of one exact code, let the nonempty set Omega(x) contain every code that can reach the decoder. In a common metric code space, for a finite sensitivity cap L, the exact robust worst-case error is \[
e_{L,\Omega}=\frac12\sup_{x,y}
\bigl[|t(x)-t(y)|-L\,\operatorname{dist}(\Omega(x),\Omega(y))\bigr]_+.
\] The infimum is attained by an L-Lipschitz real decoder. Distances between sets are infimum pairwise distances, not Hausdorff distances. To prove this, apply B to the source of pairs (x,z) with z in Omega(x), representation (x,z)↦z, and task (x,z)↦t(x). Taking the supremum over two such pairs gives the formula, and B's envelope construction proves attainment even when the closest pair of codes is not attained.

inventory.name: Good decoders for individual calibrations need not give one usable decoder
inventory.statement: Let x in [−1,1], task x, and unknown calibration theta in {−1,+1} give R_theta(x)=theta x. If theta is supplied, D_theta(z)=theta z is a gain-one exact decoder. If theta is not supplied and a single decoder must work for both calibrations, code z=1 can mean either task +1 or −1. Every common decoder has error at least one; D=0 attains one. Thus “for every calibration there is a decoder” does not establish “there is a decoder for every calibration.” One calibration bit suffices to restore exact recovery in this example and is necessary to distinguish the two conventions if otherwise indistinguishable observations are retained.

inventory.name: A finite numerical sample does not certify a uniform residual
inventory.statement:
On [0,1], any finite sample set leaves an open interval between samples. A continuous triangular spike supported in that interval can be zero at every sample and have arbitrarily large peak. Even continuity plus zero sampled residual therefore gives no finite uniform bound without a quantitative regularity assumption. If the nonnegative residual r is K-Lipschitz and every point lies within rho of a sampled point, then \[
\sup r\le\max_{\mathrm{samples}}r+K\rho.
\]

Let A be a finite action alphabet and f_a:X→X specified total maps. Let W_h be all action words of length at most h, including the empty word. Form \[
P_h(x)=(T(f_wx))_{w\in W_h},\qquad
\rho_h(x,y)=\max_{w\in W_h}d(T(f_wx),T(f_wy)).
\] For every action a, rho_(h−1)(f_a x,f_a y)≤rho_h(x,y), because each continued word is a word already tested at horizon h. Native prototype covers of radius delta_h therefore support the construction in C with updates F_(h,a)(j)=q_(h−1)(f_a(c_(h,j))). Its error along every admissible action sequence is at most sum_h delta_h.

inventory.name: An autonomous deadline has a clock cost even for a constant task
inventory.statement: Consider a system required to issue a constant task for H further transitions and then export “stopped,” without an external clock. Its H+1 remaining-time states are pairwise future-distinguishable: if h<k, after h transitions one is stopped and the other is still available. Any exact autonomous interface preserving the stop event therefore needs at least H+1 states, or ceil(log2(H+1)) fixed-length state bits. A countdown attains this bound. If stopping is scheduled externally and is not a response exported by the internal state, the constant task can instead use one state with a self-loop. These are different contracts. Charging only the maximum per-stage task alphabet hides the deadline cost in the first contract.

inventory.name: A finite predictive code is not protected against transmission errors
inventory.statement:
Suppose M initial states have future profiles separated by more than twice the allowed task error. Their transmitted b-bit words must remain distinguishable after any s bit flips. Hamming balls of radius s around these words must be disjoint, so their minimum distance is at least 2s+1 and \[
M\sum_{j=0}^{\min(s,b)}\binom bj\le2^b.
\] Otherwise one received word could stand for two incompatible forecasts. Counting the disjoint balls proves the inequality. A sufficient, deliberately inefficient construction repeats each bit of an ordinary ceil(log2 M)-bit message 2s+1 times; majority decoding corrects any total of s flips.

inventory.name: Initialization uncertainty limits the doubling predictor's horizon
inventory.statement:
For f(x)=2x mod 1 and T(x)=x, compare x=0 with x'=2^(−H−1). Their native measurement intervals of radius nu overlap whenever nu≥2^(−H−2). One shared measurement can initialize only one deterministic forecast. At time H the two tasks are 0 and 1/2, so that forecast has worst-case error at least 1/4. Consequently, a guarantee strictly below 1/4 requires \[
\nu<2^{-H-2},\quad\text{equivalently}\quad
H<\log_2(1/(4\nu))\quad(\nu>0).
\]

inventory.name: A long-time tolerance needs a contraction margin, not only a small residual
inventory.statement:
For e_(k+1)≤q e_k+delta with 0≤q<1, \[
e_k\le q^ke_0+\delta\frac{1-q^k}{1-q},\qquad
\sup_k e_k\le\max\{e_0,\delta/(1-q)\}.
\] Both bounds follow by expanding the recurrence. They are sharp: true state zero and approximate update F(z)=qz+delta, starting from z=e_0≥0, attain the recurrence and approach delta/(1−q).

inventory.name: Stable native evolution does not certify its discrete numerical update
inventory.statement:
The equation x_dot=−lambda x, lambda>0, has exact flow gain exp(−lambda t)<1 for every t>0. Explicit Euler with step h instead has gain |1−h lambda|. It contracts exactly when 0<h lambda<2. At h lambda=2 it alternates without decay; above two a small perturbation grows exponentially. For x_dot=−A x with symmetric positive-definite A, orthogonal diagonalization gives \[
\|I-hA\|_2=\max_j|1-h\lambda_j(A)|,
\]

inventory.name: Expansive steps can be allowed if the full cycle contracts

For a p-step repeating schedule e_(k+1)≤L_k e_k+delta_k, let \[
Q=\prod_{j=1}^pL_j,\qquad
B=\sum_{j=1}^p\delta_j\prod_{\ell=j+1}^pL_\ell.
\] At cycle boundaries e_((n+1)p)≤Q e_(np)+B. If Q<1, entry 69 supplies a boundary bound max(e_0,B/(1−Q)); applying the prefix recurrences gives the separate bound for each phase.

inventory.name: Residual tests need a reachable comparison tube
inventory.statement:
Let K be a nonempty exact forward-invariant subset of a metric state space, g:K→K the exact update, and F the deployed update. Suppose sup_(x in K) d(Fx,gx)≤delta and F is q-Lipschitz between all compared points in the r-neighborhood of K, where q<1. Then \[
\operatorname{dist}(Fz,K)\le q\operatorname{dist}(z,K)+\delta.
\] Compare z with a point of K arbitrarily close to its distance infimum, and use g(K)⊆K. Therefore the r-tube is forward invariant if r≥delta/(1−q). For a true trajectory x_k in K, d(Fz_k,gx_k)≤q d(z_k,x_k)+delta yields the same error bound.

inventory.name: Sampled-time closure can hide a wrong intermediate evolution
inventory.statement: On [−1,1], let the true map be f(x)=x and the reduced update be F(x)=−x, with exact encoding and decoding. Their two-step maps agree everywhere: f^2=F^2=id. A test restricted to even times reports zero residual, while at every odd time the worst task error is two. Continuous-time frequency has the same sampling issue: rotations at frequencies omega and omega+2pi/tau agree at every multiple of tau but differ between samples. These are exactly equivalent for the sampled contract; they need not be equivalent for a receiver that asks for intermediate responses.

inventory.name: A small average row error can conceal a completely wrong rare state
inventory.statement:
Let native row errors be nonnegative epsilon_x≤1 and let an evaluation distribution p assign mass alpha to one state with error one and zero error elsewhere. The average error is alpha, while the worst-case error is one. If every state has p_x≥p_min>0, then \[
\max_x\epsilon_x\le\min\{1,\overline\epsilon/p_{\min}\},
\qquad\overline\epsilon=\sum_xp_x\epsilon_x.
\]

inventory.name: Mixing improves the linear-in-time approximate-lumpability bound
inventory.statement:
Let Q be a reduced stochastic matrix with Dobrushin coefficient q=max_(z,z') TV(Q_z,Q_z')<1. Suppose every native state's aggregated row is within delta of the Q row for its current code. If mu_k is the actual observed law and nu_(k+1)=nu_k Q, then \[
TV(\mu_k,\nu_k)\le q^kTV(\mu_0,\nu_0)
+\delta(1-q^k)/(1-q).
\] The fresh discrepancy between mu_(k+1) and mu_k Q is at most delta by convexity. Q contracts TV by q: decompose a zero-mass signed difference into equal-mass positive and negative laws and average pairwise row differences. This proves the recurrence and the bound.

inventory.name: Sampled transition rows cannot be certified exactly by equality of counts
inventory.statement:
Suppose N native rows are each sampled independently n times into B observation classes. There are M=NB empirical cell probabilities. Each has variance at most 1/(4n). Chebyshev's inequality and a union bound give \[
\Pr(\max_{x,b}|\widehat p_{xb}-p_{xb}|>t)
\le M/(4nt^2).
\] Set t=2epsilon/B. With n≥M B^2/(16 alpha epsilon^2), every row has TV estimation error at most epsilon with probability at least 1−alpha. Thus a true between-row discrepancy is bounded by its empirical discrepancy plus 2epsilon. This conservative bound is explicit and requires no unjustified exact-equality inference.

inventory.name: Closure after averaging actions does not support action selection
inventory.statement: Use hidden states x0,x1 with the same current observation, and absorbing outputs g,b with different observations. Action A sends x0 to g and x1 to b. Action B sends x0 to b and x1 to g. Under a fixed policy choosing A and B with equal probability and not exporting their label, both hidden states have the same observed next law: half g, half b. The policy-averaged quotient is exact for that policy. Under action A, however, the aggregated rows have TV distance one. A controller allowed to choose A therefore cannot use the averaged-law closure certificate. Recording the action also distinguishes the two joint action/output laws. Repair: Compare aggregated rows for every selectable action, or explicitly constrain the policy and exported observations. This is a four-state finite counterexample; it does not dispute fixed-policy lumpability.

inventory.statement:
If TV(P,Q)≤delta, P(E)≥p>delta, and both conditional laws are defined, then \[
TV(P(\cdot\mid E),Q(\cdot\mid E))
\le\min\{1,2\delta/p\}.

inventory.name: The heat inverse needs an explicit precision budget
inventory.statement:
Restrict the initial state to the unit ball of the first n orthonormal eigenmodes of a nonnegative self-adjoint heat generator A. Observe z=exp(−tau A)x+e with ||e||≤nu, and request x. The exact unrestricted minimax error is \[
e_n^*=\min\{1,\nu\exp(\tau\lambda_n)\}.
\] Inverting the retained modes has norm exp(tau lambda_n), proving the upper bound nu exp(tau lambda_n); projecting its output to the unit ball cannot increase error. The constant zero decoder gives the other upper bound, one. For the lower bound, set x=±c e_n with c=min(1,nu exp(tau lambda_n)). Both can produce observed code zero, so any decoder has error at least c.

inventory.name: A full unforced heat future can cost no more than its earliest retained time
inventory.statement:
Let S(t)=exp(−tA) be the contraction heat semigroup and take the full-state receiver path (S(t)x) for tau≤t≤H, in the sup norm. For any x,y, \[
\sup_{t\in[\tau,H]}\|S(t)(x-y)\|
=\|S(\tau)(x-y)\|.
\] The value at tau supplies the lower bound; semigroup contraction supplies the upper. Ambient covering numbers of the path image and the image at tau are also equal. Evaluation at tau maps any path cover into a state cover. Conversely a state center z extends to the path S(t−tau)z, with no larger covering error.

x_j(H)=(1-e^{-1})e_j.
\] These outputs have a fixed pairwise separation, so this bounded forcing family is not compactified. Pulse amplitudes are unbounded; excluding them is an additional input contract.

inventory.name: Compact traces followed by an unbounded receiver can lose compactness
inventory.statement: On l2, let T=diag(1/j), a compact operator, and let Lambda=diag(j) with domain {z:sum_j j^2|z_j|^2<infinity}. T maps every input into this domain, yet Lambda T=identity. The composed response is bounded but not compact. Thus merely knowing that reachable traces are compact in a weak ambient norm is insufficient for an unbounded boundary operator. A sufficient repair is that T be compact into Lambda's graph-norm domain, with norm ||z||_graph=(||z||^2+||Lambda z||^2)^(1/2). Lambda is bounded from that domain into the output space, so composition is compact.

inventory.name: A stable optimum value does not imply a stable selected subspace
inventory.statement: Take S=I, K(t)=diag(1+t,1−t), |t|<1, and d=1. The minimum loss is 1−|t|, continuous and Lipschitz in t. For t>0 the unique retained line is the first coordinate axis; for t<0 it is the second. Their orthogonal projectors have operator-norm distance one. At t=0 every line is optimal, but no choice at zero makes the unique choices on both sides continuous. A tie-breaking rule therefore does not itself give a stable implementation. Uncertainty spanning the eigenvalue crossing makes the retained direction unidentified even though the optimum cost is well bounded.

inventory.name: Maximum quotient width can spend the budget on irrelevant distinctions
inventory.statement: Let X={0,1}×{0,...,7} and let the receiver task be the first coordinate. A unit-cost experiment u reveals that bit and has width one. A unit-cost distractor v reveals the second coordinate and has width three. Greedy maximization of raw quotient width chooses v, which leaves the task completely ambiguous in every resulting class. For required task pairs, u separates all 64 cross-bit pairs. v separates only the 56 with different second coordinates. Task pair coverage therefore selects u at the same budget. This does not show width is a bad objective for a receiver requesting all distinctions; it shows the task contract must determine the objective.

inventory.statement:
Let Omega(x) be the possible observations of one test. Under independent set-product uncertainty, r repetitions give Omega(x)^r. For every nonempty state family F, \[
\bigcap_{x\in F}\Omega(x)^r

\] The repeated experiment therefore has exactly the same ambiguity nerve for every finite r≥1. If two tasks can produce a common observation once, they can produce its repeated tuple, so no uniform zero-error identification improvement follows from repetition.

inventory.name: Polynomial table complexity does not mean polynomial oracle complexity in arity
inventory.statement: Consider an Interaction with one candidate-to-merge bit and m−1 independent context bits. The output for input bit zero is known to be zero. For input bit one, an oracle returns zero everywhere, or one at a single unknown context c*. Deciding whether the bit can be merged safely requires 2^(m−1) oracle queries in the zero-output worst case. After fewer queries, an unqueried context could be c*. The all-zero Interaction and that alternative give identical answers so far but require different interfaces. A deterministic always-correct algorithm cannot decide between them. This does not contradict polynomial runtime in the explicit table: the table itself has exponentially many entries in m. It exposes a concrete dependence hidden if a headline uses arity or number of branches as its input-size measure.

inventory.name: Integral route capacities sharpen the fractional erasure bound
inventory.statement:
Let m routes have nonnegative integer bit capacities and let every r=m−f survivor subset need capacity at least integer H≥0. The exact minimum total capacity of this arithmetic problem is \[
H+(m-r)\lceil H/r\rceil.
\] Sort capacities increasingly. The first r sum to at least H, so the r-th is at least ceil(H/r); each of the remaining m−r is no smaller. This proves the lower bound. Distribute H among the first r as floor(H/r) and ceil(H/r), then give every remaining route ceil(H/r). The smallest-r sum is H, proving attainment of the capacity constraints.

inventory.name: The fractional erasure bound is attainable under a centralized symbol contract
inventory.statement: Over a specified prime field F_p with p≥m, a centralized encoder holds r field symbols a0,...,a_(r−1). Form the polynomial q(z)=sum_(j=0)^(r−1) a_j z^j and send q(alpha_e) on route e at m distinct field points. Any r surviving evaluations recover all coefficients: the difference of two degree-less-than-r polynomials with r distinct zeros is zero, or equivalently the Vandermonde determinant is nonzero. The receiver quotient has p^r possibilities, so H=r log2 p semantic bits. Each route has log2 p capacity and the total m log2 p equals (m/r)H, attaining the fractional lower bound. Any r−1 routes cannot distinguish all p^r messages by cardinality. This is the standard polynomial erasure code, proved here in the declared finite contract. It assumes centralized access, classical field symbols, known erasure locations, and no corruption of surviving symbols.

inventory.name: Approximate relational closure needs a loss for empty successors
inventory.statement: Choose a declared penalty a>0. On nonempty compact successor sets use d_a(A,B)=min(d_H(A,B),a); adjoin the empty set with d_a(empty,A)=a for every nonempty A and d_a(empty,empty)=0. This is a metric: capping a metric preserves triangle inequality, and the new-point inequalities follow directly from all nonempty distances being at most a. If one current representation fibre contains both an empty successor set and a nonempty one, its minimum radius over all allowed successor-set centers is exactly a, rather than a/2. Every center is either empty or nonempty and therefore has distance a to at least one member; all distances are at most a. Thus any uniform error strictly below a forces availability to be exact on every fibre.

inventory.source_statement: The proposed cancellation is realizable. The six three-link staple paths surrounding an interior link use 18 distinct links; they share vertices but no link variables. Therefore one can prescribe the six staple products independently by setting two links on each path to identity and setting the third appropriately. For a chosen neighbor f, reserve its staple as the affected path. On the other five paths prescribe \[  S_j=\cos(2\pi j/5)I+i\sin(2\pi j/5)\sigma_3,  \qquad j=0,\ldots,4. \] These are SU(2) matrices and \sum_jS_j=0. On the affected path, hold its other two links fixed at identity and change only f between I and -I. The central link then sees H=+I or H=-I, respectively. Orientation reversal preserves this sign change. This construction is available for every neighboring f; the supremum defining each coefficient may use its own conditioning configurations. Writing U=\cos\theta I+i\sin\theta\,\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma, the two densities are \[  q_\beta^\pm(U)=Z(\beta)^{-1}e^{\pm\beta\cos\theta},  \qquad Z(\beta)=2I_1(\beta)/\beta,\quad Z(0)=1. \] Their positive likelihood-difference region is \cos\theta>0. Haar measure gives marginal (2/\pi)\sin^2\theta\,d\theta, hence \[  \mathcal C(\beta)=\frac{2}{\pi Z(\beta)}  \int_0^{\pi/2}(e^{\beta\cos\theta}-e^{-\beta\cos\theta})\sin^2\theta\,d\theta,  \qquad c_{ef}\ge\mathcal C(\beta). \] Point conditioning is legitimate for this continuous, everywhere positive finite-temperature specification; nearby configurations approach the same values.

inventory.source_statement: Let X=\cos\theta under Haar measure. Its density is 2\sqrt{1-x^2}/\pi on [-1,1]. Then \[  \mathcal C(\beta)  =\frac{\mathbb E\sinh(\beta|X|)}{\mathbb E\cosh(\beta X)}  =2\mathbb P_\beta(X>0)-1, \] where \mathbb P_\beta tilts Haar measure by e^{\beta X}. Differentiating gives \[  \mathcal C'(\beta)=2\operatorname{Cov}_\beta(\mathbf1_{X>0},X)>0. \] Strict positivity follows because both half-intervals have positive mass and the conditional mean on the positive half exceeds the conditional mean on the negative half. Thus the inverse used in DD-2269 and DD-2270 is well defined for values in (0,1). Expansion of the numerator and denominator gives, more precisely, \[  \mathcal C(\beta)=\frac4{3\pi}\beta-\frac7{90\pi}\beta^3+O(\beta^5). \] For large β, the negative-half numerator is 2/(\pi\beta)[1+O(\beta^{-2})], while Z(\beta)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,e^\beta\beta^{-3/2}[1+O(\beta^{-1})]. Therefore \[  \mathcal C(\beta)=1-2\sqrt{2/\pi}\sqrt\beta\,e^{-\beta}[1+O(\beta^{-1})]. \] In particular each neighboring coefficient tends to one and the interior row sum tends to 18.

inventory.name: Qubit unitary/precession model
inventory.statement: Let $H=\hbar\Omega\sigma_z/2$, $U(t)=\exp(-iHt/\hbar)$, and $\rho=(I+r\cdot\sigma)/2$. Computing $U\rho U^*$ rotates $(r_x,r_y)$ by angle $\Omega t$ and leaves $r_z$ fixed. Equivalently $\dot r=\Omega e_z\times r$, so $d|r|^2/dt=2\Omega r\cdot(e_z\times r)=0$. For $|r|=1$ the state remains pure. The page shows this state vector, its circular orbit at fixed polar angle, and the three observable expectation values. A $\sigma_z$ observation alone cannot distinguish transverse phases. The page describes the density-matrix/observable model and does not assert that the Bloch vector is an electron position or that a single measurement reveals its components exactly.

inventory.name: Kepler/gravity/tidal model
inventory.statement: For $0\le e<1$, $a>0$, and $\mu>0$, let $n^2=\mu/a^3$ and solve $E-e\sin E=nt+M_0$. Since $1-e\cos E>0$, the mean anomaly determines a unique eccentric anomaly on each unwrapped period. Then $$x=a(\cos E-e),\qquad y=a\sqrt{1-e^2}\sin E.$$ Differentiating the anomaly equation gives $\dot E=n/(1-e\cos E)$. With $r=a(1-e\cos E)$, a second differentiation of $x,y$ gives $\ddot{\mathbf x}=-\mu\mathbf x/r^3$. The specific energy is $-\mu/(2a)$ and angular momentum magnitude is $\sqrt{\mu a(1-e^2)}$. The differential acceleration tensor is $\mu(3\hat r\hat r^\top-I)/r^3$, with radial eigenvalue $2\mu/r^3$ and transverse eigenvalues $-\mu/r^3$. The page shows a radial tidal direction and computes its current magnitude. Newton iteration solves the anomaly equation numerically and reports its residual. The model is a weak-field classical test-particle system. It is not an Einstein-equation solution or a derivation of gravity from information.

inventory.statement: Every global continuous scalar factor of a homeomorphism of R^n has a continuous scalar refinement encoding its entire past, with an increasing or decreasing homeomorphic update on an interval.

inventory.name: Mutual long-return obstruction for scalar factors
inventory.statement: If nearby points can approach x then reach y under even forward iterates, and conversely, every continuous scalar closed code identifies x and y.
inventory.assumptions: J1 setting; both endpoint limits exist; even nonnegative iterate counts allow order-reversing refined updates.
inventory.evidence: B20 BM20-J2: full written proof; exact executable checks where applicable in section 8. Independent review remains open. B21: BM21-J1 supplies the complete native long-return relation for each Jordan chain; BM21-J2 applies the obstruction in every chain length.

inventory.name: Exact continuous three-state scalar Jordan optimum
inventory.statement: For n=3,d=1 every continuous sampled-autonomous scalar encoder satisfies R(a,b,0)=R(a-prime,-b,0). The exact Lp trajectory optimum is ||O_2,T|| for every 1<=p<=infinity; x3 attains it.

inventory.name: Explicit nonlinear improvement over closed linear Jordan codes
inventory.statement: For n=4, epsilon=T=1, R=d+(c^3-3bcd+3ad^2)/300000 is invariant. Decoder t^3R/6 beats every closed linear scalar code by more than 10^-10 in squared worst-case L2 error.

inventory.statement: An m-state deterministic causal predictor exists iff an m-cell cover satisfies initial coverage, uniform availability, successor containment and task-radius bounds. Exact current-state encoding uses partitions.

inventory.statement: Finite rational points have a rational minimum-ball center and squared radius, certified by at most p+1 affinely independent boundary points with nonnegative barycentric weights.

gates.requirement: Inventory the distinct primitive/rule families and every named T/W/FI/SH support identifier in the selected current sources.
gates.evidence: 23 byte-pinned sources in the manifest, with all 23 hashes replayed in the 23 October readiness supplement; named-ID maps and six-label inventory. Historical completeness remains a separate gate.
gates.closure_test: Validate schema, all source/dependency links, exact named-ID coverage and classification totals.

gates.requirement: Recover missing primary transcripts/proofs and reconcile every historical DD/lineage ID and supersession.
gates.evidence: RA/R explicitly disclose unrecovered DD history; G includes summary-only AG/Hodge/string/JOINT lineages; exact GRDE-008 grammar not recovered.
gates.closure_test: A source manifest contains every retained original statement/proof, stable ID, version and explicit retired/replaced disposition; no memory reconstruction substitutes for a missing source.
gates.priority: Required only for all-history completion claim

gates.requirement: Obtain independent proof/certificate review of specified release claims.
gates.evidence: Sources report internal written proofs and finite checks; SHU/SHB explicitly disclaim independent peer review.
gates.closure_test: Independent reviewer or formal checker examines named statements and proof artifacts, resolves concrete objections and records the review scope.

gates.requirement: Complete theorem-specific prior-art comparison, including equivalent formulations outside project vocabulary.
gates.evidence: BEN first crosswalk and R/F attribution exist; neither certifies exhaustive historical priority. The 23 October comparison supplies an explicit T55-C7R-to-labelled-bisimulation reduction under full-product assumptions and a targeted primary-source crosswalk. The broader novelty gate remains open.
gates.closure_test: Written exact-statement crosswalk records matches, reductions, genuinely different hypotheses/conclusions and unresolved searches.

gates.requirement: All core roles typed; principal statements have hypotheses, proofs/counterexamples and fixed dependencies.
gates.evidence: F Edition 1.1, M T01–T55, R current amendments; no blanket smooth/physical portability. Readiness supplement: all T01–T55 direct proof bases mapped explicitly; the pre-existing ledger did not encode all source dependencies. Do not equate the ledger graph with a complete formal proof graph.
gates.closure_test: Retain the frozen core and corrected hypotheses. Reopen only for a concrete contradiction, missing hypothesis or new stronger audited statement.

gates.requirement: Exact finite refinement, rational projector certificate and prescribed nonlinear repair classes have concrete constructions.
gates.evidence: R/I show the algorithms, proofs and reported verification; current audit checks consistency of the inventory, not every source program. B18 adds exact finite correlated, fragmentation, causal-safety and rational Pauli solvers with independent finite oracles and certificate replay. B20 adds exact invariant-cover synthesis with rational Euclidean outputs and 2,166 independent mode/budget comparisons. B23 adds 15 exact quantum optimality certificates and a finite response-tree implementation with 49,104 replay checks, under a separately proved uniform decay bound.
gates.closure_test: For a new instance, supply the native inputs and replay its exact certificate with the documented tolerances.

gates.status: Scoped contracts resolved; six broader extensions open
gates.requirement: Solve only the explicitly chosen extension contracts rather than declare all possible mathematics finished.
gates.evidence: B18 resolves finite correlated/fragmentation contracts. B20 resolves continuous n=3 scalar Jordan, finite all-output causal synthesis and full-algebra quantum bounds in all finite dimensions; refutes universal linear Jordan optimality and universal smooth minimum algorithms. B21 solves the Jordan long-return calculation for all chain lengths and certifies a stronger four-state nonlinear interval; the unrestricted optimum remains open. B23 proves finite algebraic quantum computability/capability formulations and a general decay construction, and disproves universal approximate infinite-horizon optimization. Its general QE procedure is not executed.
gates.closure_test: Resolve the unrestricted remaining Jordan optima and specified global, nonlinear and native infinite/physical contracts; evaluate quantum formulas where an explicit envelope is required. Universal algorithmic demands already disproved must not be relabelled as achievable open tasks.

gates.requirement: Declare state, law, receiver, tasks, admissibility, interventions and continuation; use the applicable native theorem.
gates.evidence: R/M explicitly define Core/SOE/ACE/IRE/UKE/HDE/GHSE and preserve GRDE-008 scope.
gates.closure_test: Each admitted application instantiates every required contract field and meets the theorem conditions; the framework need not invent one universal response law.

gates.requirement: For each extension application, certify domains, operation order, witnesses, regularity, metrics and physical realization as requested.
gates.evidence: Generic contracts and examples exist; exact GRDE primary grammar/validation implementation and every arbitrary native instance are not supplied.
gates.closure_test: A typed model satisfies its declared composition and acceptance laws, including dead ends, joint stochastic laws and one common physical decoder where required.

gates.requirement: Give complete native statements/proofs for every promoted research family and keep candidates separate.
gates.evidence: Some fibre/lattice/cut identities have direct proofs; many G entries are active candidates or summary-only lineages. P18 now supplies eight complete scoped proof families, explicit counterexamples and exact finite checks. Native deployment, other research candidates and missing historical sources remain unresolved.
gates.closure_test: Retain the eight P18 scoped contracts and corrected embedding contract; establish native conditions, recover missing original definitions and prove the remaining structured, analytic and transport hypotheses.

gates.requirement: Measure a useful added result against a strong native baseline with reproducible inputs and uncertainty.
gates.evidence: BEN is a real-data reproduction, explicitly no pipeline improvement; FAR/rounding scope corrections are included. Six illustrative model equations are supplied, implementation not tested. B18 supplies small deterministic timing cases and exact finite oracles, but no external comparator or demonstrated practical advantage.
gates.closure_test: Predeclare task, comparator, cost/error metric and holdout data; show repeatable improvement or record no added advantage.

gates.requirement: Supply a native model, self-adjoint evolution, actual vacuum, state metric, response and certified regulated results.
gates.evidence: SH8/SH9/SHM/SHU/SHB provide those equations and written results.
gates.closure_test: Use original normalization and source hypothesis restrictions; do not equate this standard native branch with a unique new universal Steadman law.

gates.requirement: Define RD type, units, composition, receiver/gauge/covariance behavior and a justified conservation/transport law.
gates.evidence: A qualitative hypothesis and specific unitary distinction invariant exist; no universal density/current or additive law is derived.
gates.closure_test: A precise object and equations yield a proved invariant/transport theorem and observable normalization; fixed-receiver counterexamples are respected.

gates.requirement: Derive or select the actual physical generator/action and account for the full energy metric and omitted information.
gates.evidence: Analytic smoothing of supplied Hamiltonians is defined, but does not uniquely select physical real-time dynamics.
gates.closure_test: Prove a nontrivial monotonic/extremal consequence of a specified physical law and test it without fitting the desired conclusion.

gates.requirement: Supply an independent predictive action/constitutive law or a proved derivation showing exactly which existing equations the principles select.
gates.evidence: eta_R is defined; Efficiency Force and a unique combined universal dynamics remain unproved/underdetermined.
gates.closure_test: All fields, parameters, constraints and initial/boundary data determine a well-posed model with a discriminating prediction; no circular ideal-reference fitting.

gates.requirement: Extend the actual operator/locality/return estimates along a physically matched scaling trajectory and every required scale.
gates.evidence: Volume-uniform SU(2) strong coupling is established internally; one-step blocking and a fixed-spacing form exist. No weak-coupling trajectory is supplied.
gates.closure_test: Close the renormalized operator class, propagate state metrics/memory and obtain a positive physical-energy liminf after all losses and rescaling.

gates.requirement: Construct the nontrivial continuum theory, its observables/vacuum/Hilbert realization and required axioms; prove the physical gap in that theory.
gates.evidence: SHU fixed-spacing subsequential form is limited; SH8 gap transfer has unproved continuum identification/convergence hypotheses.
gates.closure_test: Controlled a->0, volume->infinity, physical coupling/units, appropriate reconstruction/relativistic axioms, nontriviality and gap; general compact simple-group scope if claiming the full target.

gates.requirement: Derive an upstream background scale, coupling or mixing relation rather than reproduce the known mass Gram matrix.
gates.evidence: SH-EW2 is standard-QFT translation; finite-total dilution and orientation-minimization no-go remain.
gates.closure_test: A parameter relation/selection rule follows before experimental fitting and survives the stated infinite-volume/gauge constraints.

gates.scope: Additional field, gravity, particle or matter claims
gates.requirement: Supply the native spaces, action/equations, stress/energy/charges, covariance, causality and excitation interpretation.
gates.evidence: The corpus explicitly prohibits treating a completion fibre or persistence label as a particle, force, energy scale or trajectory.
gates.closure_test: An exact typed physical bridge plus independently distinguishable observable consequence is derived; no label-only identification.
gates.priority: Only if those physical claims are made

gates.requirement: Identify calibrated parameters, observational identifiability and a preregistered discriminating test.
gates.evidence: No independent universal Steadman prediction is derived by the inspected sources; existing lattice calculations inherit the supplied native dynamics.
gates.closure_test: Specify measurable quantities, units, confounders, uncertainty, effect size and acceptance/rejection rule; compare against known dynamics on independent data.

changes.topic: Exact test for lattice metric use
changes.old: A monotone potential defines a discrepancy, but monotonicity alone does not license the triangle inequality or metric route propagation.
changes.new: For finite monotone v on a lattice, pseudometric iff supermodular; metric iff also strictly increasing on strict comparisons. The strict-monotone example on subsets of {1,2} has triangle values 4,1,1.
changes.evidence: P18 §7; exhaustive comparison of triangle/supermodularity over 719 finite monotone potentials.
changes.action: Add G-P18-Metric; strengthen G-Curvature native contract and retain route metric/Lipschitz obligations. This fills a criterion without claiming the earlier source already asserted a false metric.

changes.topic: Gaussian merge and branch-normalization contract
changes.old: Disjoint record labels and a common constant do not by themselves certify independent Gaussian block addition or correct branch scores.
changes.new: Require conditional block independence and fixed covariances. Include log det Sigma in zeta or retain a branch-specific normalizer. Covariance 1/2 gives true quadratic 4/3 versus 2; variances 1 and 4 give a density factor 2 at zero.
changes.evidence: P18 §2; exact rational residual checks for 7 block subsets and 175 parameters; explicit covariance/normalizer witnesses.
changes.action: Add G-P18-Streaming and explicit native sufficient-statistic fields; keep deletion and hard-constraint limitations visible.

changes.topic: Polynomial Jordan scope is not arbitrary continuity
changes.old: The interior continuous Jordan problem was unresolved; a polynomial proof alone could be misreported as settling it.
changes.new: BM18-J1–J2 prove the exact n=3,d=1 scalar-polynomial and continuous-first-integral optimum. Arbitrary continuous noninvariant factors remain open. Follow-up C15 removes this restriction for the original continuous n=3,d=1 case.
changes.evidence: B18 §2; antipodal-plane proof; explicit four-state invariant blocks naive dimension extension.
changes.action: Add scoped theorem entries and retain the original continuous-encoder obligation.

changes.topic: Quantum normalization and reference locator
changes.old: The conservative recovery estimate used a Theorem 3.1 locator; normalized operator-system defect can be mistaken for physical noise magnitude.
changes.new: The cited arXiv approximate upper bound is Theorem 1. Full-algebra normalized kappa is 0 or 2; qubits have sharp upper envelope delta<=kappa/2, with no positive lower envelope at fixed nonzero kappa.
changes.evidence: B18 BM18-Q1–Q5; Beny arXiv:0907.4207 Theorem 1.
changes.action: Correct the citation in the active Research Edition and separate unamplified, diamond and normalized quantities.

changes.topic: Infinite prediction needs causal implementation hypotheses
changes.old: Total boundedness of future profiles may suggest a finite infinite-horizon causal implementation without an additional stability argument.
changes.new: Irrational rotation has compact profile space but no finite autonomous predictor with uniform error below one. Contraction provides an explicit sufficient alternative.
changes.evidence: B18 BM18-A1–A3; finite safety certificates and exact rotation obstruction.
changes.action: Retain cover-versus-machine distinction and require the declared causal/native conditions.

changes.new: The finite deterministic join-lifting criterion and the finite fragmentation complexity/FPT question now have full proofs and implementations. External benchmarks remain G3.

changes.topic: Continuous three-state Jordan gap closed

changes.new: An ordered history refinement and mutual-return obstruction prove the exact optimum for all global continuous scalar sampled factors.

changes.topic: Universal linear optimality refuted
changes.old: The exact closed linear formula was an upper bound and a possible candidate for the general nonlinear optimum.
changes.new: A globally invariant scalar polynomial in the four-state chain strictly beats the entire closed linear scalar class, with an explicit rational margin.

changes.action: Do not extend the linear optimum formula to all nonlinear codes.

changes.topic: Finite causal output catalogue restriction removed
changes.old: The finite synthesizer optimized only over a specified finite output catalogue.
changes.new: Invariant-cover enumeration with exact minimum-ball certificates optimizes over all real Euclidean outputs and all infinite histories.
changes.evidence: B20 BM20-C1–C3; 577 native/task cases and 2,166 independent mode/budget comparisons.
changes.action: Distinguish overlapping memory covers from closed current-state partitions; retain infinite/native constraints.

changes.topic: Higher-dimensional quantum scope expanded
changes.old: Sharp normalized-defect results were limited to qubits, with a general cap of two.
changes.new: The cap is sharply 2(1-1/r) for algebra rank r. Full-algebra recovery pairs are classified in every finite dimension; binary tasks have an exact primal/dual.
changes.evidence: B20 BM20-Q1–Q3, including a complex-operator trace-projection norm proof.
changes.action: Keep the unamplified norm and normalized defect unchanged; leave general proper-algebra intermediate-defect geometry open.

changes.topic: Effective hypotheses and universal limits made explicit
changes.old: Compactness gave existence without an effective repair modulus; a general smooth minimum algorithm could be presumed possible.
changes.new: Compact semialgebraic coefficient contracts have an effective modulus. A universal exact minimum-dimension algorithm for computable smooth inputs is impossible. A diagonal infinite-dimensional native class has a constructive predictor.
changes.evidence: B20 BM20-N1, G1 and I1.
changes.action: Require the exact effective input and native hypotheses; do not treat a no-go theorem as a solution of every restricted model.

changes.new: The stale prefix is removed; the actual B18 proof and exact verification references remain.

changes.topic: Jordan long-return obstruction quantified in every chain length
changes.old: The continuous obstruction had been proved explicitly for the three-state scalar interior case.
changes.new: Hermite interpolation classifies all native long-return endpoint pairs and yields forced scalar identifications and Lp lower bounds for every Jordan chain length.
changes.evidence: B21 BM21-J1–J2, including the odd-chain parity condition and rational bridge implementation.
changes.action: Use the proved prefix size k(n); do not infer a general exact optimum or stronger middle-coordinate antipodal symmetry.

changes.topic: Four-state nonlinear upper bound strengthened and family scope quantified
changes.old: The explicit nonlinear proof improved squared error over the linear optimum by only a conservative margin above 10^-10.
changes.new: A rational cubic encoder and fixed decoder certify squared error <=1.2949. Every invariant polynomial of degree <=3 with that decoder has squared error >=1.2948. The general continuous lower bound remains (4+sqrt(13))/6.
changes.evidence: B21 BM21-J3–J4; exact Gram/LDL and rational weighted-state certificates.
changes.action: Separate the global continuous interval from the narrower fixed-decoder cubic-family interval; retain the unrestricted optimum as open.

changes.topic: Finite quantum scope and endpoint attainment
changes.old: Proper-algebra geometry had only solved examples and conservative bounds.
changes.new: An exact finite algebraic formulation determines recovery optima and defect-error sections. Normalized defect slices need not be closed, so endpoint attainment is explicitly tested.
changes.action: Separate proved computability from an executed QE calculation or efficient solver.

changes.topic: Universal approximate causal optimization is impossible
changes.old: The infinite-carrier boundary could be read as a universal optimization task waiting for a general algorithm.
changes.new: A binary rational task on the fixed transition n->n+1 encodes a halting distinction between one-state optimal errors 0 and 1/2.
changes.evidence: B23 BM23-I2
changes.action: Record the negative theorem; pursue explicitly restricted native classes such as BM23-I1.

changes.new: The ten BM Hypothesis rows are six research boundaries, three optional candidates and one retired proposal. The two conditional rows are application bridges. None is silently promoted.

BM_readiness.name: The scalar decoder theorem does not yet include uncertain codes
BM_readiness.statement:
Let the task values t(x) be bounded real numbers. Instead of one exact code, let the nonempty set Omega(x) contain every code that can reach the decoder. In a common metric code space, for a finite sensitivity cap L, the exact robust worst-case error is \[
e_{L,\Omega}=\frac12\sup_{x,y}
\bigl[|t(x)-t(y)|-L\,\operatorname{dist}(\Omega(x),\Omega(y))\bigr]_+.
\] The infimum is attained by an L-Lipschitz real decoder. Distances between sets are infimum pairwise distances, not Hausdorff distances. To prove this, apply B to the source of pairs (x,z) with z in Omega(x), representation (x,z)↦z, and task (x,z)↦t(x). Taking the supremum over two such pairs gives the formula, and B's envelope construction proves attainment even when the closest pair of codes is not attained.

BM_readiness.name: A finite numerical sample does not certify a uniform residual
BM_readiness.statement:
On [0,1], any finite sample set leaves an open interval between samples. A continuous triangular spike supported in that interval can be zero at every sample and have arbitrarily large peak. Even continuity plus zero sampled residual therefore gives no finite uniform bound without a quantitative regularity assumption. If the nonnegative residual r is K-Lipschitz and every point lies within rho of a sampled point, then \[
\sup r\le\max_{\mathrm{samples}}r+K\rho.
\]

BM_readiness.name: An autonomous deadline has a clock cost even for a constant task
BM_readiness.statement: Consider a system required to issue a constant task for H further transitions and then export “stopped,” without an external clock. Its H+1 remaining-time states are pairwise future-distinguishable: if h<k, after h transitions one is stopped and the other is still available. Any exact autonomous interface preserving the stop event therefore needs at least H+1 states, or ceil(log2(H+1)) fixed-length state bits. A countdown attains this bound. If stopping is scheduled externally and is not a response exported by the internal state, the constant task can instead use one state with a self-loop. These are different contracts. Charging only the maximum per-stage task alphabet hides the deadline cost in the first contract.

BM_readiness.name: A finite predictive code is not protected against transmission errors
BM_readiness.statement:
Suppose M initial states have future profiles separated by more than twice the allowed task error. Their transmitted b-bit words must remain distinguishable after any s bit flips. Hamming balls of radius s around these words must be disjoint, so their minimum distance is at least 2s+1 and \[
M\sum_{j=0}^{\min(s,b)}\binom bj\le2^b.
\] Otherwise one received word could stand for two incompatible forecasts. Counting the disjoint balls proves the inequality. A sufficient, deliberately inefficient construction repeats each bit of an ordinary ceil(log2 M)-bit message 2s+1 times; majority decoding corrects any total of s flips.

BM_readiness.name: Closure after averaging actions does not support action selection
BM_readiness.statement: Use hidden states x0,x1 with the same current observation, and absorbing outputs g,b with different observations. Action A sends x0 to g and x1 to b. Action B sends x0 to b and x1 to g. Under a fixed policy choosing A and B with equal probability and not exporting their label, both hidden states have the same observed next law: half g, half b. The policy-averaged quotient is exact for that policy. Under action A, however, the aggregated rows have TV distance one. BM_readiness.name: Polynomial table complexity does not mean polynomial oracle complexity in arity
BM_readiness.statement: Consider an Interaction with one candidate-to-merge bit and m−1 independent context bits. The output for input bit zero is known to be zero. For input bit one, an oracle returns zero everywhere, or one at a single unknown context c*. Deciding whether the bit can be merged safely requires 2^(m−1) oracle queries in the zero-output worst case. After fewer queries, an unqueried context could be c*. BM_readiness.name: Integral route capacities sharpen the fractional erasure bound
BM_readiness.statement:

BM_readiness.name: The fractional erasure bound is attainable under a centralized symbol contract
BM_readiness.statement: Over a specified prime field F_p with p≥m, a centralized encoder holds r field symbols a0,...,a_(r−1). Form the polynomial q(z)=sum_(j=0)^(r−1) a_j z^j and send q(alpha_e) on route e at m distinct field points. Any r surviving evaluations recover all coefficients: the difference of two degree-less-than-r polynomials with r distinct zeros is zero, or equivalently the Vandermonde determinant is nonzero. The receiver quotient has p^r possibilities, so H=r log2 p semantic bits. Each route has log2 p capacity and the total m log2 p equals (m/r)H, attaining the fractional lower bound. Any r−1 routes cannot distinguish all p^r messages by cardinality. This is the standard polynomial erasure code, proved here in the declared finite contract. It assumes centralized access, classical field symbols, known erasure locations, and no corruption of surviving symbols.
